messages:
morgan: :rotating_light: noticed elevated 500s from eu-west canary after the blue->green swap 2m ago. Errors are concentrated on /v1/generate and some embedding requests. Dash shows 30% error rate for eu-west-canary pool. rolling-deploy tag: release/2026-03-15-22:10.

pagerduty-bot: Paging @sre-liz (oncall) — a high-sev incident has been created: INC-2026-045.

incident-bot: Incident INC-2026-045 created by deploy-bot: eu-west canary failures after traffic shift. Severity: SEV2. Channels: #incidents, #eng-runtime, #support.

sre-liz: ack, on it. morgan can you paste the deploy id and the edge logs you see?

morgan: deploy id: release/2026-03-15-22:10 sha: d4f7a2. stacktrace sample from edge logs: 
```
[ERROR] 2026-03-15T22:12:11Z proxy: 500 upstream_write_error service=runtime-canary-eu-west host=gen-1
[WARN] kv-cache: miss key=prefix:abc123
```

morgan: Also seeing a weird split: ~40% of requests routed to green (healthy) respond fine, ~60% to blue return 502/500. But DNS/weighting for geo has EU routing pinned to blue in some POPs. TTLs were set to 15s during rollout.

devon: Checking envoy headers — seeing a `x-rl-routing` header rewrite on the blue variant that adds a trailing slash to the host header. That causes our proxy matcher to pick the older upstream pool which is still flagged as draining. Suspect proxy header normalization + DNS sticky TTL causing sessions to stick to draining backends.

ben-engineer: I can confirm backend `runtime-canary-eu-west-blue` has drain flag set but still in LB pools due to stale route table on edge instances in eu-central POPs. We pushed flag to drain during the swap but some edges didn't pick up the config.

product-tom: Support is getting escalations from three customers in EMEA — two have timed-out requests, one reports partial responses. We should include a customer-impact note in the incident.

sre-liz: immediate mitigation plan: 1) flip feature flag to revert traffic to green-only for eu-west; 2) run targeted evict on stale edge POPs; 3) temporarily raise LB health-check aggressiveness. If flip takes >2m, we escalate to rollback the release. Anyone object?

devon: I'm on the kill-switch for the rollout flag. Doing: 
```
# kill the canary routing flag
curl -X POST -H "Authorization: Bearer $OPS_TOKEN" \
  https://controls.redwood.internal/flags/release/2026-03-15-22:10/kill
```

devon: flag flip executed at 22:15:06Z. Confirming route table recomputation...

morgan: Cloudwatch/metrics show traffic shifting to green within ~30s for most POPs, but eu-central POPs still showing 50/50 split. TTL on edge DNS was 15s but some resolver caches in region are sticky.

ben-engineer: Running targeted restart on edge instances in eu-central: `kubectl rollout restart daemonset/edge-proxy -n platform --selector=pop=eu-central`

incident-bot: Action logged: flag_kill executed by devon at 2956782506.

sre-liz: OK, while restarts are in flight let's also remove the draining backend from LB backend set as a hotfix: 
```
# remove backend from LB (one-off)
rbctl backend detach --pool runtime-eu-west --instance runtime-canary-eu-west-blue-03
```

morgan: removal accepted, LB rebalanced. Errors falling to ~4% overall, eu-central down to ~8%. Support confirmed one of the customers recovered, others still intermittent.

product-tom: Customer-impact summary for page: ~3 enterprise customers affected intermittently for ~18 minutes, degraded generation latency, some 500s. No data exfiltration.

devon: I see logs indicating a proxy header rewrite rule introduced in the canary config that expected hostnames without trailing slashes; in combination with a stale edge config, it routed to legacy pool. We'll add a test for header normalization to the canary validation.

ben-engineer: Opening a PR for the validation: `eng-runtime/pr/482-add-host-header-check`.

sre-liz: Current status: mitigation succeed, traffic stabilized to green-only across POPs. I'm going to mark incident as mitigated but keep it open for postmortem.

incident-bot: Incident INC-2026-045 status changed: mitigated at 2956782580 by sre-liz.

morgan: quick notes for postmortem: root cause = header-rewrite+partial config propagation resulting in cross-pool routing during blue->green flip. Contributing factors: low TTL + some resolver stickiness + missing canary validation for host-header normalization.

product-tom: I'll coordinate comms with support to send a summary to affected accounts.

devon: Handoff: I'm taking ownership for the night followup and long-form postmortem. I'll schedule a blameless postmortem tomorrow at 09:00 UTC.

sre-liz: thanks. I'll add runbook updates: add step to verify header rewrite rules and to confirm edge config propagation before shifting >20% traffic.

morgan: tagging action items: [DEV] PR 482 for header check, [SRE] add runbook step, [OPS] change LB removal safeguard, [PM] customer comms.

pagerduty-bot: Notification: @devon assigned follow-up on INC-2026-045.

devon: logging handoff here: last check 22:23Z, system stable. leaving channel to oncall rotation.

sre-liz: oncall handoff note: escalate to next oncall if errors >5% for 5m.

morgan: closing thread for now — will attach logs and graphs to the incident.

ben-engineer: adding a short-term monitoring alert to detect header-rewrite mismatch patterns.

incident-bot: INC-2026-045 updated: mitigated -> postmortem pending.
